title: A same-function-field DVR centred at a nongeneric point
statement: Let $Z$ be an integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point], and put $L=\kappa(\eta)=\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$, its function field [def-sc-function-field]. For every point $z\in Z$ with $z\ne\eta$, there exist a discrete valuation subring $A\subseteq L$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field exactly $L$, and a morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] such that $a$ maps the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ to $z$ and $a|_{\operatorname{Spec}L}$ is the canonical generic-point morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z$ (with the identity map on $L$). Moreover, under the canonical injection $\mathcal O_{Z,z}\hookrightarrow L$, one can choose $A$ to contain $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ with $\mathfrak m_A\cap\mathcal O_{Z,z}=\mathfrak m_{Z,z}$; thus $A$ dominates this local ring.

source.place: Tag 054F, properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-specialization-dvr, (2) for the strict specialization eta to z and the identity extension L/L; constructive affine argument in limits.tex Tag 0208, limits-lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-proper, using algebra.tex Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $z$ with $R$ Noetherian, from the defining locally Noetherian cover. Put $B=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ and let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ represent $z$. The affine-stalk localization theorem identifies $B$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}$, so localization permanence makes $B$ Noetherian. The integral-scheme stalk theorem gives that $B$ is a domain and that the canonical map $\rho_z:B\hookrightarrow L$, $s_z\mapsto s_\eta$, is injective with fraction field $L$. Regard $B$ as this subring of $L$.

source.place: Tag 054F, properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-specialization-dvr, proof: the local ring and its image in the chosen field; affine localization and Algebra Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Let $c:\operatorname{Spec}B\to Z$ be the canonical morphism. Its image is all generalizations of $z$. Since $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Z$, this image contains both $\eta$ and $z$. If $B$ were a field, $\operatorname{Spec}B$ would have one point, contradicting $z\ne\eta$. Thus $B$ is not a field. Since $B$ is a local domain, its maximal ideal is therefore nonzero: if it were zero, every nonzero element would lie outside the maximal ideal and would be a unit, making $B$ a field.

source.place: Tag 054F, proof, the non-field assertion marked details omitted; Schemes Tag 01J7, schemes-lemma-specialize-points.

proof.text: Apply the existing same-field local-domain DVR lemma to $B\subseteq L$. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1 and 2. Obtain a discrete valuation subring $A\subseteq L$ containing $B$, with fraction field $L$ and $\mathfrak m_A\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$. Write $i:B\hookrightarrow A$ and $j:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ for the morphism induced by $A\hookrightarrow L$.

source.place: Tag 054F, proof, choose a DVR dominating the image; Algebra Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, identity field extension L/L.

proof.text: Define $a=c\circ\operatorname{Spec}(i):\operatorname{Spec}A\to Z$. Under a map of spectra a prime maps to its inverse image. Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}(i)$ sends $\mathfrak m_A$ to $i^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)=\mathfrak m_B$, and $c$ sends $\mathfrak m_B$ to $z$. Thus $a$ has the required closed-point value and the already obtained containment and contraction give domination.

source.place: Tag 054F, proof, induced morphism; Schemes Tag 01J6 and canonical morphism 02NA.

proof.text: By clause (1) of the canonical-morphism theorem, $c^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ for the affine open $U$ of step 1. Thus $a\circ j$ factors through $U$. The affine description of $c$ and functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ show that $a\circ j$ is induced by $R\to B\to A\to L$. This composite sends $r$ to $\rho_z(r_z)=r_\eta$. The generic point belongs to $U$, and the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}=\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z$ has on $U$ precisely the same ring map $r\mapsto r_\eta$. The affine-spectrum correspondence therefore makes the two morphisms equal. Explicitly every element of $L$ is $r_\eta/s_\eta$ with $r,s\in R$, $s\ne0$; the resulting generic field map sends this fraction to itself. Hence it is the identity of the fixed field $L$, not merely an unspecified field isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 054F (2) with the identity extension L/L; Schemes canonical morphism 02NA, affine descriptions at z and eta; compare the identical-field construction in Limits Tag 0208.
